critical_bugs: pickle.load() used on session files without safety checks; pickle deserialization can execute arbitrary code if data is tampered with or untrusted.
File handles opened via open(slam_file, 'rb') and open(motive_file, 'rb') are never closed, causing resource leaks (file descriptor exhaustion) in production loops.
warnings: Broad 'except Exception as e' suppresses specific error types, making debugging and monitoring difficult.
No type checking on deserialized data; calling .get() will raise AttributeError if pickle payload is not a dict.
sys.argv input lacks path sanitization, allowing directory traversal (e.g., '../') which could read/write outside intended session directories.
recommendations: Replace pickle with JSON or Protocol Buffers for data interchange to eliminate deserialization vulnerabilities.
Wrap all file operations in 'with open(...) as f:' context managers to guarantee resource cleanup.
Validate and resolve session_dir against a known safe base path using Path.resolve() and .is_relative_to().
Implement structured logging instead of silent exception catching, and handle specific exceptions explicitly.
